question.problem: Given that $p(x)=2x$ and $q(x)=7{x}^{4},$ what is ${lim}_{x\to \infty }(p(x)\cdot q(x))?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply the two functions, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(p(x)\cdot q(x)) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(2x\cdot 7{x}^{4}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }((2\cdot 7){x}^{1+4}) \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }(14\cdot {x}^{5}) \\  & =14\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{5}\end{aligned}
$$

The graph $y={x}^{5}$ is power function with an odd positive power and therefore has the property that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{5}=\infty .
$$

Multiplication by the positive constant $14$ does not affect the limit at infinity. So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}14\cdot {lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{5}={lim}_{x\to \infty }{x}^{5}=\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
{lim}_{x\to \infty }(14{x}^{5})=\infty .
$$
